book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer

indicators.note: 'sound' asks for a word that is heard rather than seen, so the next word is replaced by something pronounced the same

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language; spelt here as it sounds

explanation.surface: A commander heads up a reliable Irish military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' just puts the officer at the front. 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it signals that Erse is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce someone is to compel them by pressure, so the verb is a synonym of force.

clue.text: Man finds a route to European capital

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a route

explanation.surface: A traveller works out how to reach a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' tells you the capital comes first, with 'a route' attached after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard is a male first name, and crosswords often define any forename by man or woman.

clue.text: If upset, fit a new hearth

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned over
to fit a new one is to replace the old

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed with their fireplace decides to install a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If upset' reads as a condition about someone being annoyed; it is just the two letters of if turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth is the floor of a fireplace, and by extension the whole fireplace itself.

clue.text: Main expert has aged so terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly or wrongly, so the letters are scrambled out of order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A leading authority has grown old very badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like principal, but it is the old poetic word for the sea, so a main expert is an experienced sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is a veteran sailor, someone thoroughly expert on the ocean or main.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sweet white wine made from the ... grape, as in Alsace
second meaning: the capital city of Oman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' with its exclamation mark sounds like an old-fashioned cry of approval for the wine; it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a grape and wine grown in France and the chief city of Oman.

clue.text: I gaol man in error. What a bloomer!

indicators.note: in error means mistakenly placed, so these letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A judge admits jailing a man by mistake, and someone remarks on the blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which fits the wrongful jailing; here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnolia is a tree or shrub grown for its large showy flowers, so it is literally a bloomer.

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone has an unusual longing to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' reads as odd or remarkable, but it is only the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart and fashionable, a synonym of chic.

clue.text: He complies when dispatched by HM

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sent means dispatched
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A loyal subject does as he is told when sent on a royal errand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places the royal initials after the rest. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the usual crossword stand-in for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An assenter is one who assents, that is a person who agrees or goes along with something.

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a day or two'
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A fracture shows up in a ship or a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a split in the hull, but it is a joke, as in 'make a crack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, and a one-liner is a joke or quip told in a single sentence.

clue.text: African leader wins time in opposition

indicators.note: a leader is the one in front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: the first letter of African
to gain is to win
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An African head of state keeps power for a while despite resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African leader' suggests a president; it is just the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the preposition for being opposed to something, so it means in opposition.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chain of mountains
second meaning: the distance something can extend

explanation.surface: The hills are close enough to get to.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a line of peaks and the scope or extent that something can cover.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at once, without thinking

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining the adjective phrase, as in 'it got out of hand'

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts read as one event, something suddenly going wild; they are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both immediately and dismissively, and also beyond control.

parts.note: us is the object form of the pronoun we

indicators.note: middle points to the central letter of the word it is joined to, keeping only that one

parts.note: the clue word middlemen's splits into middle and men; this is the centre letter of men

explanation.surface: Consumers complain about how middlemen take advantage of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' reads as a protest, but it is a grammar note: the object form of we. 'Middlemen' splits into middle and men.
explanation.definitionFit: To use someone is to exploit them, so use as a noun can mean exploitation.

clue.text: Listen to Cockney promotions? Not with these!

parts.note: hear without its H, as a Cockney drops it
plugs are pieces of publicity for a product

explanation.surface: Someone is told to ignore adverts delivered in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (East Londoners) traditionally drop their aitches. The definition is a joke: these are what you cannot listen with.
explanation.definitionFit: Earplugs block sound, so you cannot hear with them in, which the exclamation teasingly implies.

clue.text: She lives with a handsome Parisian

parts.note: is means exists or lives
taken as written
bel is French for handsome or beautiful

explanation.surface: A woman shares her home with a good-looking Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is not a pronoun but stands for any woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female first name, so crosswords can define it simply as she.

clue.text: First dire concoction from a wok

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up from ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The opening attempt at cooking produced an awful dish from the wok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' fits the cooking scene, which hides that it is the signal to mix letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-fried food is cooked quickly in a wok, so anything from a wok is likely stir-fried.

clue.text: Make summary for criminal of little brain

parts.note: a con is a convict
dense means stupid

explanation.surface: Writing a short report about a dim-witted crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of little brain' echoes Winnie-the-Pooh, the 'Bear of Very Little Brain'. Summary here is the adjective meaning brief.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a text is to shorten it, that is to make it brief or concise.

clue.text: Golly! Sounds like a bird's cry

indicators.note: sounds like says the word before is matched by pronunciation, not spelling

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like golly

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a noise that resembles a bird call.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech the R of cor is silent, so it rhymes with caw.
explanation.definitionFit: A caw is the harsh call of a crow or rook, a bird's cry.

clue.text: He's detested for writing articles about Frenchman

definitions.note: the whole phrase stands for 'he's anathema'

indicators.note: about means around, so the string of words wraps round the single letter that follows

parts.note: the articles an, a, the and a written out in a row
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A writer is hated for producing pieces about a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces; it means the grammatical articles an, a and the. The M goes in just before the final a.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anathema to you is intensely loathed, so 'he's anathema' means he's detested.

indicators.note: a word that can move to and fro reads identically in either direction

parts.note: cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: Rubbish being carted back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition supplies the word, and the rest only adds that it reads the same backwards. 'Junk' could also be the Chinese boat sailing to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for tasteless rubbish or junk.

clue.text: Show respect to people producing 'The Archers'

parts.note: to bow is to show respect
men are people

explanation.surface: A tribute to the team behind The Archers, the long-running BBC radio soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress archers up as the radio programme; it simply means people who shoot with bows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen are archers, people who shoot arrows from a bow.

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say nothing' reads as a vow of silence; 'I' is the definition and the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I and means the self, so the pronoun is a fair definition.

clue.text: Butterfly saw Pinkerton under his control, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the red ..., a common butterfly

definitions.text: saw Pinkerton under his control, maybe
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a senior naval officer, who might command a lieutenant like Pinkerton

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Madame Butterfly watching Pinkerton, the US Navy lieutenant in Puccini's opera; 'maybe' warns that the second definition is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a family of butterflies and the top rank of naval officer, under whom a lieutenant would serve.

parts.note: surface reading: started working frantically hard
setter's reading: overdrive is a car's top gear, so moving into it means changing to a higher gear

explanation.walkthrough: The everyday idiom for frantic activity also has a literal motoring sense, a shift into a higher gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To gear up is to prepare for intense effort, and literally to move into a higher gear like overdrive.

indicators.note: in says one name sits inside the word that follows it

parts.note: the end is the final part
Sue Barker, the British tennis player and broadcaster

explanation.surface: Someone trailed Sue Barker in a tennis final.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Barker was a British tennis star who later fronted BBC Wimbledon coverage and the quiz show A Question of Sport, which suits the final.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a result, so ensued is a synonym of followed.

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
a microwave is a kind of oven

explanation.surface: A pair own a microwave that has been checked for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proven has been tried and shown to work, so it has been tested.

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or in all directions, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone was warned about offering lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it means concerning; it signals a rearrangement of the word before.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is the process of being taught, which is what education means.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be in harmony
second meaning: the sound of a bell

explanation.surface: Someone says yes to a proposal of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The engagement picture misleads: the ring is the sound of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas that chime are in accord, and a chime is the ringing tone of a bell or clock.

parts.note: surface reading: a big animal that pries into other people's business
setter's reading: the beast's name comes from the Greek word for nose, and its horn sits on its snout

explanation.walkthrough: Nosy here means all about the nose, not inquisitive: the animal's name literally means nose-horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino is a huge thick-skinned African or Asian mammal with one or two horns on its snout.

parts.note: in means at home
sides are teams

explanation.surface: Teams playing at home must show courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' wants to mean courage in the sporting scene; here it is the literal innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Insides is informal for the stomach and bowels, which is what guts means literally.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a legate is an envoy, especially of the Pope

explanation.surface: An order to strip troops of rank after they faced down an envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confronting' puts the soldiers face to face with, and so in front of, the envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move down to a lower rank or division, a synonym of demote.

clue.text: Chap had taken an age to win Ivy

parts.note: he is a male person, a chap
'd is the shortened form of had, as in he'd
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A man took ages to woo a woman called Ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, whose botanical name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the Latin genus name for ivy, the evergreen climbing plant.
